requirement:
For every `{test}` reference in a project source file, including one in a
requirement or example declaration, the evidence file for the referenced
requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover
the reference's file and line. An `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{fixme}` reference alone
MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. `{impl}` and `{cite}` sources
remain discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`;
`{fixme}` acknowledgments are supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` and tracked by
{cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`. Habeas MUST report every uncovered
reference requiring coverage with its role, full name, source file, and line
number.
rationale:
structural: No implementation roots are supplied, and `requirements.references.evidence_coverage` states no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. I read the requirement text and the three cited requirements, `requirements.authoring.reference_index`, `requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` and `requirements.ci.reference_set`. I did not read any source code.

I checked each clause for a structural reading:
- "For every `{test}` reference ... the evidence file ... MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover the reference's file and line." This describes what the evidence file contains. Any implementation that yields the same coverage check, such as a different data structure, algorithm or module split, behaves identically and satisfies the clause. It is observable behavior.
- "An `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{fixme}` reference alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source." This is a negative behavioral rule about when coverage is demanded. It prescribes no type or interface.
- "`{impl}` and `{cite}` sources remain discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`; `{fixme}` acknowledgments are supplied under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` and tracked by {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`." These are citations that give context. The cited requirements are separate declarations assessed on their own text. This requirement does not delegate any implementation to them.
- "Habeas MUST report every uncovered reference requiring coverage with its role, full name, source file, and line number." This fixes the content of the report: its fields are role, full name, file and line. It does not fix a signature, type or library. A report that carries the same information from a differently shaped internal structure behaves the same.

Every clause therefore specifies only observable behavior, and tests supply the evidence for it.

behavioral: I derived three obligations from `requirements.references.evidence_coverage`. The reviewed tests cover each one. I did not read implementation source.

1. **Every `{test}` reference needs a covering input, wherever it appears.** This includes references in requirement or example declarations.
   - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[source_references_are_covered_by_evidence_inputs]` has a `{test}` in `md/notes.md` covered by an outline input for those lines. It expects no errors.
   - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cited_example_with_a_test_and_matching_evidence_validates]` has a `{test}` inside a declaration in `md/rules.md` and a `{test}` in `src/main.rs`. It checks four cases:
     - A requirements-text input covers the declaration's reference, including after the declaration moves.
     - An unselected `{test}` outside the declaration is reported.
     - Emptying inputs makes the declaration's reference fail.
     - Emptying the example's inputs makes the `src/main.rs` reference fail.
   - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reports_unknown_references_and_uncovered_lines]` shows that coverage is per line. One of two identical-text lines is covered and the other is reported.
   - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable]` and `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[selector_anchors_are_covered_by_inputs_selecting_the_node_or_an_ancestor]` cover `:test:` anchors. An input selecting the node, an ancestor, or the whole file satisfies the anchor. A different node or an uncovered anchor is reported.

2. **`{impl}`, `{cite}` and `{fixme}` alone must not require an input.**
   - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[only_test_references_require_recorded_source_coverage]` has a `{cite}`, an `{impl}` and a `{test}` with empty inputs. Exactly one "no input covers" error is produced, and it is for the `{test}`. Nothing is reported for the `{cite}`. A changed `{impl}` body causes no error.
   - `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[editing_or_adding_a_fixme_makes_evidence_stale_without_requiring_source_reads]` asserts that no "no input covers {fixme}" error appears for a new `{fixme}` and for an edited one.
   - `src/sites.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_fixme_inside_a_site_belongs_to_that_sites_review_only]` asserts that no "no input covers {fixme}" error appears.
   - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_false_determination_fails_only_its_own_record_with_its_rationale]` has `{impl}`, `{test}` and `{cite}` references to `rules.ready` in a declaration. Only the false determination is reported.

3. **Every uncovered reference must be reported with role, full name, file and line.**
   - `reports_unknown_references_and_uncovered_lines` asserts the exact message `no input covers {test}` followed by the reference, the file and the line. That contains the role, name, file and line.
   - `cited_example_with_a_test_and_matching_evidence_validates` asserts the role `{test}`, the name `rules.ready`, the file and the line. It also asserts the file and line for the example's reference.
   - `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[fixme_does_not_hide_stale_inputs_or_uncovered_references]` adds an uncovered `{test}` in `other.txt` and asserts `no input covers` with the file and line.

The other requirements cited in the subject (`requirements.authoring.reference_index`, `requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` and `requirements.ci.reference_set`) are context only. The subject's text states no independent obligation under them that needs a test here.

All the relevant tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no unmarked relevant test and no gap.

text: :::{req} evidence_coverage
For every `{test}` reference in a project source file, including one in a
requirement or example declaration, the evidence file for the referenced
requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover
the reference's file and line. An `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{fixme}` reference alone
MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. `{impl}` and `{cite}` sources
remain discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`;
`{fixme}` acknowledgments are supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` and tracked by
{cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`. Habeas MUST report every uncovered
reference requiring coverage with its role, full name, source file, and line
number.
:::{req} reference_index

`lookup_requirements` MUST accept an optional requirement-name glob and return matching requirement and example node IDs and their data. With no selection it lists all requirements and named examples. The agent can inspect implementation, citation, test, and acknowledgment targets through `outgoing_edges`. Reading the returned node through `read_node` records its contents.
:::{req} fixme_inputs
For a requirement or example assessment, the initial request MUST include every
valid named `{fixme}` reference to the subject found under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except a reference inside one of
the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, in this
form:
```text
Acknowledgment {
file: String,
item: String,
body: String,
issues: Array<{ reference: String, state: "open" | "closed" }>,
`file` and `item` MUST locate the containing source by project-relative path and
outline selector, using `<root>` for a whole file. `body` MUST contain the
reference's complete fenced commentary without its fences or source-comment
delimiters, including its option lines, redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. `issues` MUST give every distinct issue
its `:github:` lines name, in their order, with state supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`. Acknowledgments MUST be ordered by
file and position in the file and MUST carry no line numbers or containing
implementation source.
The locations and bodies MUST be protected against staleness by the reference-set
digest under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`; the acknowledgment MUST NOT
create an outline input merely to cover its containing source. Actual reads of
that source MUST still be recorded under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. Sources MUST satisfy
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; an inaccessible acknowledgment
MUST be reported before inference.
Terminology definitions referenced by an acknowledgment's body MUST contribute
their complete, transitive declarations to the mandatory input set under
{cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` and MUST be recorded as
definition inputs. Only the acknowledgment's body MUST contribute these
dependencies; its containing implementation source MUST NOT be supplied merely
to discover them.
:::{req} reference_set

A definition's reference set MUST consist of its current incoming `{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` edges, except a `{fixme}` inside a site of the definition under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles` and
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors`: for each edge, its role and the file and
outline selector of the node the reference belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, or of the anchored file or
node, and, for a fenced reference in a source outside the book, the words of
its body under the word rule of {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
`{cite}` references MUST NOT contribute. The reference-set digest MUST be
the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of those entries in sorted order,
so it does not depend on line numbers or on the order references are found.
For a structural assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, the digest MUST additionally
include a versioned structural-assessment marker. A record predating structural
assessment MUST therefore be stale, including a legacy record with a wildcard
review version. Other assessments MUST retain their existing digest encoding.
Authoring MUST record the digest of the reference set it supplied, and
validation MUST recompute it and report a changed reference set as stale
evidence. Adding or removing an `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{fixme}` reference or anchor,
changing its role, editing its commentary, or moving it to a different node
MUST therefore make the evidence stale even when no recorded input changed; moving a reference within
the node it belongs to MUST NOT.
